raw_response:
I'm a 50-year-old farmer in Quzhou, been working these fields since I was 20. I didn't finish primary school — had to help at home — but I've been farming this same land for 30 years and I know what works here. My farm is only 8.5 mu, not big, and there are seven mouths to feed at home. My son and daughter-in-law work off-farm in the county town, so they send some money back, but it's not much. That means I rely mostly on family labor — me, my wife, and sometimes my younger daughter when she's not busy.

My land is split up. I've got 5 mu where I do wheat-maize double cropping — that's my bread and butter. Then 2.5 mu of cotton, which brings in cash but is a lot of work. The remaining 1 mu I plant mungbean, mostly for our own eating and a little to sell. I don't have much cash to throw around, so I have to think carefully about every yuan.

Right now it's spring. The wheat I planted last October is coming up green and strong. This year the winter wasn't too cold, so the wheat looks okay. I need to topdress it soon — I usually put down about 10 kg of urea per mu at jointing. My neighbor Lao Zhang did 15 kg last year and his yield was good, but fertilizer prices went up again, so I'll stick to 10 kg per mu. That's 50 kg of urea for the 5 mu. I'll spread it by hand when the soil is moist enough. I'll irrigate twice before harvest — once after the topdressing and once at flowering if it doesn't rain. The pump electricity isn't cheap, about 40 yuan each time for the 5 mu, so I watch the sky closely.

For cotton, I'll plant in about 10 days, around April 20th, when the soil warms up. I buy Bt cotton seed — about 1.5 kg per mu, costs me around 45 yuan per mu. I use plastic mulch because everyone around here does, and it keeps the weeds down and helps the seedlings get going in this unpredictable spring weather. The plastic film costs another 30 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, I spread about 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base before planting, and then topdress with urea twice — once at squaring and once at flowering. Cotton needs water but not too much, so I'll irrigate twice, maybe three times if it's very dry in July. I'll spray pesticide three or four times because the bollworm always comes, even with Bt cotton. That's maybe 80 yuan per mu in chemicals.

The maize I'll plant right after wheat harvest in mid-June — usually I only have about five or six days between harvest and planting, so there's no time to waste. I hire a combine for the wheat (custom harvest, about 50 yuan per mu) and then I plant maize the next day or two. I use hybrid seed, about 2.5 kg per mu, costs around 35 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, I put compound fertilizer in the row at planting — about 40 kg per mu — and then topdress with urea at the big-flare stage, about 12 kg per mu. Maize needs water, especially at flowering, so I'll irrigate twice if there's no rain. 

The mungbean I plant on my 1 mu plot in mid-May. It's an easy crop — I just broadcast the seed, about 3 kg per mu, and scratch it in. I put down a little phosphorus fertilizer, maybe 20 kg of superphosphate, and that's about it. Maybe one irrigation in July if it's very dry. I harvest in late August and the family eats most of it.

Labor is tight. My wife and I do most of the work. For wheat, we need about 10 family days total for the whole season (fertilizing, irrigating, spraying, harvesting help). Cotton is the worst — it needs about 25 family days for 2.5 mu because of all the spraying, pruning, and picking. I don't hire labor for cotton picking anymore because it's too expensive — the family does it ourselves over two months, picking every few days. For maize, about 12 family days. Mungbean is easy, maybe 5 days. I do hire a combine for wheat harvest and sometimes a tractor for plowing if I'm short on time between crops — that's about 150 yuan total in hired machine work.

My total budget for inputs this year is about 3,200 yuan. I could spend more, but my son says they might need money for my grandson's school fees, so I keep a reserve. I'd rather apply a little more fertilizer than risk a bad yield — losing half a crop hurts a lot more than wasting 100 yuan on extra urea.

I expect about 450 kg per mu of wheat this year if the weather holds, about 500 kg per mu of maize, maybe 220 kg per mu of cotton lint if the bollworms don't get too bad, and 100 kg of mungbean from my 1 mu.
